AgentPipeline.query default extra_args={} is one dict shared by every run in the process, and upstream MELON writes masked_tool_call_bank / masked_tool_emb_bank into it, so the bank would leak across runs and threads (and into the port). The upstream pipeline is a thin AgentPipeline subclass that passes a fresh {} per run (class _FreshExtra); no upstream decision logic is touched
module namespace: print and pprint replaced by no-ops (debug output only, thread noise)
module registered in sys.modules (dataclass needs it); module namespace: helpers _txt, _blk, _HUB_CLIENT injected
llm handed to MELON is wrapped by _StrToBlocks, which converts str message content to v1.2 content blocks before each llm.query (upstream builds the masked conversation with str content)

pipeline wiring as README (ToolsExecutionLoop([ToolsExecutor(), MELON(llm, threshold=0.1)]), AgentPipeline([SystemMessage, InitQuery, llm, tools_loop])), but with harness SYSTEM_MESSAGE and max_iters=12 exactly as every other defense of this study
upstream detect() zips a set (masked_tool_call_bank) with a list (masked_tool_emb_bank), so pairing depends on set iteration order (PYTHONHASHSEED); kept as upstream
